\textbf{Source.} Tadelis (2013), \emph{Game Theory: An Introduction}, Exercise 5.5 ``Public Good Contribution'', p.~96 {[}PDF p.~115{]}. Answer in the source: none (the preface, p.~xiii, says about half of the exercises are solved on Princeton UP's website). Reproduced verbatim.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{Public Good Contribution:} Three players live in a town, and each can choose to contribute to fund a streetlamp. The value of having the streetlamp is 3 for each player, and the value of not having it is 0. The mayor asks each player to contribute either 1 or nothing. If at least two players contribute then the lamp will be erected. If one player or no players contribute then the lamp will not be erected, in which case any person who contributed will not get his money back.

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\alph{enumi}.}
\item
  Write out or graph each player's best-response correspondence.
\item
  What outcomes can be supported as pure-strategy Nash equilibria?
\end{enumerate}
\end{quote}
